title: Composition and pullback of the underived sheaf of sections with proper support
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring, and let $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to Z$ be separated morphisms locally of finite type of schemes [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-proper-morphism] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For a sheaf $F$ of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], define $f_!^{\mathrm{supp}}F$ to be the subsheaf of $f_*F$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] whose sections on an etale $V\to Y$ are those $s\in F(X\times_Y V)$ whose support (the closed subset where the geometric germs of $s$ are nonzero [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]) is proper over $V$. A closed support is given its reduced induced closed subscheme structure [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme], and properness means properness of this scheme over $V$. Fibre products are as in [def-pc-fibre-product]. Then
$$g_!^{\mathrm{supp}}f_!^{\mathrm{supp}}F=(gf)_!^{\mathrm{supp}}F$$
as subsheaves of $(gf)_*F=g_*f_*F$, with the identification induced by equality of the underlying sections. For proper $f$ one has $f_!^{\mathrm{supp}}F=f_*F$; for an open immersion $f$ one has $f_!^{\mathrm{supp}}F=f_!F$, the extension by zero of [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero]. These identifications are natural and $\Lambda$-linear. For any Cartesian base-change square of $f$ with projections $a:X'\to X$, $b:Y'\to Y$ and map $f':X'\to Y'$, the ordinary pullback comparison $b^{-1}f_*F\to f'_*a^{-1}F$ restricts to the canonical isomorphism $b^{-1}f_!^{\mathrm{supp}}F\cong f'_!{}^{\mathrm{supp}}a^{-1}F$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. The support-composition identifications commute with these pullback comparisons: for two stacked Cartesian squares, the comparison for $gf$ equals the successive comparisons for $g$ and $f$ after the displayed support-composition identifications.

proof.text: The support of a section is closed: its complement is the largest open on which it vanishes, by [lem-sc-etale-section-zero-open]. For a pullback $u:T'\to T$, [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ] identifies the germ of the pulled-back section at $\bar t'$ with the original germ at $u\bar t'$. Thus its support is exactly $u^{-1}\operatorname{Supp}(s)$. The statement applies to underlying abelian sheaves; [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] supplies precisely the same inverse image on constant-$\Lambda$ modules. Germwise, $\operatorname{Supp}(s+t)\subseteq\operatorname{Supp}(s)\cup\operatorname{Supp}(t)$ and $\operatorname{Supp}(\lambda s)\subseteq\operatorname{Supp}(s)$, since a sum or scalar multiple of zero germs is zero. The support of zero is empty.

proof.text: For an etale $V\to Y$, the proposed proper-support sections form a $\Lambda$-submodule of $F(X_V)$: finite unions of proper closed supports are proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base-union-preimage](1), and their closed subsets are proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base-properties](2). Restriction preserves the condition by step 1 and [lem-cbc-closed-proper-support-locality](1). For a covering $\{V_i\to V\}$, glue compatible sections in the ordinary direct-image sheaf [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Their glued support pulls back to their individual supports by step 1, so [lem-cbc-closed-proper-support-locality](2) makes it proper over $V$. Uniqueness is inherited from $f_*F$. This constructs the required subsheaf. A linear sheaf morphism sends a zero germ to zero, so its image support is a closed subset of the old support and remains proper by the same closed-subset lemma. Thus the construction is a functor on module sheaves.

source.place: Tag 0F4X (lemma-f-shriek-separated), subgroup, restriction and gluing arguments

proof.text: All base-changed maps in the argument are locally of finite type: on affine charts, base change replaces a finitely generated algebra $B=A[b_1,\ldots,b_n]$ by $B\otimes_AC$, generated over $C$ by $b_i\otimes1$. Composite maps are locally of finite type since finite generating sets for $B/A$ and $D/B$ together generate $D/A$, using the affine-open definition [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Separatedness is preserved by base change by [lem-weil-pbc-separated-base-change]. For composition, $\Delta_{gf}$ factors through $X\times_YX$: its first factor is $\Delta_f$, and the second is the pullback of $\Delta_g$ along $X\times_ZX\to Y\times_ZY$. The second factor is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]; two closed immersions compose, since their affine maps are surjective ring maps and the composite of surjections is surjective [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Hence $gf$ and all needed base changes are separated. The same affine quotient description gives local finite type for closed subschemes used below.

proof.text: Fix $W\to Z$ etale, write $X_W=X\times_ZW$, $Y_W=Y\times_ZW$ and $f_W:X_W\to Y_W$, and let $s\in F(X_W)$. Put $T=\operatorname{Supp}(s)$. Suppose that $T$ is proper over $Y_W$, so $s$ defines a section of $G=f_!^{\mathrm{supp}}F$ on the etale object $Y_W\to Y$. By [lem-weil-pbc-proper-closed-image] its image $I=f_W(T)$ is closed. Over $Y_W\setminus I$, the original section has all germs zero and is zero by [lem-sc-etale-section-zero-open]; hence the section of $G$ has zero germs there. Conversely, if the germ of this section of $G$ at a geometric point over $y\in Y_W$ is zero, apply [lem-sc-etale-section-zero-open] to $G$ itself: there is a Zariski open neighbourhood $O\subseteq Y_W$ of $y$ on which this section is zero. The inclusion $G\subseteq f_*F$ implies $s|_{X_W\times_{Y_W}O}=0$. By step 1, $T\cap f_W^{-1}(O)=\varnothing$. If $y$ belonged to $I$, a point of $T$ over $y$ would belong to this intersection, a contradiction. Therefore the support of the section of $G$ is exactly $I$. This supplies the omitted support-image calculation of 0F50 using actual Zariski zero neighbourhoods, without a filtered-colimit argument or ordinary direct-image stalk base change.

source.place: Tag 0F50 (lemma-f-shriek-composition), first paragraph: details omitted; support-image calculation expanded

proof.text: If $T$ is proper over $W$, then its reduced closed scheme maps properly to $Y_W$ by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-over-separated], because $Y_W\to W$ is separated (step 3). Its image $I$ is closed and proper over $W$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base-properties](3). Therefore step 4 shows $s\in(g_!^{\mathrm{supp}}f_!^{\mathrm{supp}}F)(W)$. Conversely, membership in that module says that $T\to Y_W$ is proper and its closed image $I$ is proper over $W$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base-union-preimage](2) to the proper map $T_{\mathrm{red}}\to Y_W$ of schemes locally of finite type over $W$ (step 3) and the closed subset $I$. Its inverse image is all of $T_{\mathrm{red}}$, so $T$ is proper over $W$. This avoids making an unjustified scheme factorization through the reduced image. These two implications prove equality on every $W$ inside the ordinary direct image. The equality is literally the identity on sections and hence is natural, linear and compatible with restriction.

source.place: Tag 0F50 (lemma-f-shriek-composition), second paragraph; equivalent inverse-image argument for the converse

proof.text: For proper $f$, $X_V\to V$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change], and each closed reduced support in $X_V$ is proper over $V$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper](c). Thus every section qualifies and $f_!^{\mathrm{supp}}F=f_*F$ with the identity inclusion.

For an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow Y$, map the presheaf $j_{p!}F$ of [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero] to $j_!^{\mathrm{supp}}F$. If $V\to Y$ factors through $U$, send its section to the same section on $U\times_YV=V$; its support is closed in $V$ and hence proper over $V$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper](a). For the zero presheaf value use zero. These maps respect restriction, so the universal property [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] produces a linear map $j_!F\to j_!^{\mathrm{supp}}F$. Inside $U$ it is the identity on the original germs; [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-stalks](1) says it is a stalk isomorphism there. Outside $U$, a section of the target on $V$ has support $T\subseteq U_V$ proper over $V$, whose image in $V$ is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-closed-image] and misses the given point. On the open complement of that image the section is zero, by step 1, so its germ is zero. The source stalk is zero there by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-stalks](2). Hence [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-iso-on-geometric-stalks] makes the map an isomorphism on underlying sets; its inverse is linear since it inverts a bijective linear map objectwise. Its composite into $j_*F$ is the canonical extension map by its presheaf construction. This proves the open specialization without the extra etale-sheet arguments needed for a general separated etale morphism.

Consider the stated square of $f$, and put $G=f_!^{\mathrm{supp}}F$ and $H=f'_!{}^{\mathrm{supp}}a^{-1}F$. Construct a linear sheaf morphism $\alpha:G\to b_*H$ directly. On an etale object $U\to Y$, [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] gives $(b_*H)(U)=H(U\times_YY')$. Send $s\in G(U)\subseteq F(X\times_YU)$ to its pullback on $(X\times_YU)\times_YY'=X'\times_{Y'}(U\times_YY')$. The coefficient sheaf here is the restriction of $a^{-1}F$, by the unit-compatible inverse-image compositors [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units] and the module inverse-image construction [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. Step 1 identifies its support with the inverse image of the support of $s$, and [lem-cbc-closed-proper-support-locality](1), for the base change $U\times_YY'\to U$, makes that support proper over $U\times_YY'$. Thus the section belongs to $H(U\times_YY')$. Pullback respects restrictions, sums and scalars, so these maps define $\alpha$. The adjunction $b^{-1}\dashv b_*$ of [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact](3) gives its adjoint $\beta_f:b^{-1}G\to H$. Composing $\alpha$ with $b_*H\to b_*f'_*a^{-1}F$ gives the sectionwise pullback map defining the ordinary comparison; the adjunction hom-bijection therefore shows that $\beta_f$ followed by $H\hookrightarrow f'_*a^{-1}F$ is the ordinary comparison restricted to $b^{-1}G$. For a geometric point $\bar y':\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y'$, put $\bar y=b\bar y'$. The inverse-image stalk formula [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ] identifies the source stalk with $(f_!^{\mathrm{supp}}F)_{\bar y}$. By [lem-cbc-proper-support-geometric-stalk] the source and target stalks identify with compactly supported sections on $X_{\bar y}$ and $X'_{\bar y'}$ respectively. These schemes are canonically equal as fibre products over the same $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$; their coefficient sheaves agree under inverse-image composition [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units], and [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] supplies the constant-$\Lambda$ action. The adjunction identity $b_*\beta_f\circ\eta_{b,G}=\alpha$ says that $\beta_f$ sends the unit pullback of every representative $s\in G(U)$ to the pullback section defining $\alpha_U(s)$. The germ-compatible inverse-image stalk isomorphism identifies the germ of that unit pullback with the original germ of $s$. The two fibre restriction maps therefore send it to the same section, since the two composites from the geometric fibre to $X\times_YU$ coincide. Every source stalk element is such a germ, and the new stalk lemma specifies restriction as its isomorphism; thus the stalk comparison is the identity on compactly supported fibre sections. Thus it is bijective. By [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-iso-on-geometric-stalks], $\beta_f$ is an isomorphism, with a linear inverse. No torsion, finite-ring or Noetherian hypothesis is used.

proof.text: For the stacked Cartesian squares write the horizontal projections $a:Z'\to Z$, $b:Y'\to Y$, $c:X'\to X$ and the vertical maps $f',g'$. The ordinary exchange for $gf$ equals $g'_*\operatorname{Ex}^0_f\circ\operatorname{Ex}^0_g f_*$: this is the adjunction-pasting equation [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting](2), applied to the inverse-image composition squares, whose unit-compatible compositors are those of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units]. The module adjunctions have those same underlying units and counits by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact](3). Restrict this equality to $a^{-1}(gf)_!^{\mathrm{supp}}F$. Step 5 identifies support composition by identities on sections; step 8 constructs each support exchange as the restriction of the corresponding ordinary exchange. Both resulting paths have the same composite into $(g'f')_*c^{-1}F$. Its support-subsheaf inclusion is injective objectwise, so the two paths are equal already in $(g'f')_!^{\mathrm{supp}}c^{-1}F$. All these equalities are natural and linear: section maps are linear, the inclusions are linear, and the factorizations are unique. The same identity-on-sections argument gives associativity and identity composition identifications.
